argument_summary: The supportable position is not that certification is cleanly resolved on disclosure, but that certification is defensible on a qualified basis from the existing record. The admissible evidence shows aggregate launch readiness passes by 2.2 percentage points and the launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents. The same record also shows the grant compliance review segment is below target by 1.3 percentage points, that the segment is named in two agency grant commitments, and that legal review on disclosure remains open. Public governance guidance supports deployment with documented evaluation results, limitations, and ongoing monitoring, so the strongest compliant framing is certification with explicit caveat rather than a clean no-issue conclusion.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not the basis for compliance. At most, the existing record supports avoiding unnecessary escalation if the packet is limited to a qualified certification rationale and does not overclaim resolution of the disclosure issue.
claims_about_policy: The stated policy cuts against any claim that the non-core or 5% traffic characterization resolves materiality. Under the policy text, named launch use cases and pending legal review keep the materiality question live. But the current record does not itself prove that certification must be denied; it shows that any certification defense must be narrow and must not claim that no material weakness disclosure is required. The admissible evidence therefore supports caveated compliance more than either full exoneration or immediate escalation on the present record.
concessions: A clean claim that certification is fully compliant under the materiality policy is not supported by the admissible record.
A claim that no material weakness disclosure is needed is not supported because the affected segment is tied to two agency grant commitments and legal review is still open.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness, but do not by themselves resolve the disclosure question.
